headline: High-risk shared filesystem and server-datastore coupling make Flowise→MinerU prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and ingest uploaded files, while MinerU accepts local file inputs and exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible bridge where Flowise outputs or uploaded content can be fed into MinerU and then reused as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into MinerU inputs without provenance checks
IF MinerU MCP responses are treated as instructions by Flowise flows
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every handoff file
Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into Flowise prompts
Use a separate folder for untrusted documents
Require manual review before any prompt reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and can read/write the server filesystem; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, images, and OCR text. If both share a workspace or uploaded files, sensitive content can flow from Flowise into MinerU processing and back into outputs. MinerU is offline-oriented, but the shared-file path still makes leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or upload bucket
IF Flowise chatflow inputs contain secrets or regulated documents
mitigations: Separate storage locations per agent
Restrict MinerU to non-sensitive documents
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Delete shared temp files after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem=true and shared_state_with_other_instances via server datastore, while MinerU is read-only on filesystem and does not write git state. Overlap exists mainly on shared inputs, not on the same mutable resource set, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The pair still needs coordination if they share a workspace, but the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF Flowise flows mutate shared datastore records that MinerU also reads
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize access to any shared folder
Avoid concurrent runs on the same documents
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise can generate or transform content that MinerU then parses from documents or OCR text, and MinerU exposes MCP/API surfaces that may consume upstream outputs. If MinerU treats Flowise-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade from one agent into the other without verification. The profiles do not show a built-in validation gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests Flowise-generated text as source material
IF downstream automation acts on MinerU extractions without human review
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Compare extracted fields against the original document
Flag low-confidence OCR or parsing results
Require human approval before any action-taking step
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention policies. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while MinerU is documented as private/offline and processes document files, so a compliance issue is only plausible if regulated data is routed into MinerU or retained in Flowise logs. The other agent is not cited because no explicit mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Flowise logs or chatflow outputs
IF MinerU processes data subject to a residency or retention rule
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Set short log retention on Flowise
Delete processed documents after use
Document a data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls
